newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan says Uganda priming itself for invasion.
newsitem.headline: Sudan says Uganda priming itself for invasion.

text.p: Sudan said on Sunday that Uganda was getting ready to join invading Eritrean and Ethiopian forces and was massing arms and troops at the border to fight Khartoum's Islamist government.

"A huge buildup of Ugandan, Eritrean and Tigrayan (Ethiopian) forces...have completed their plans to launch an attack on southern Sudan from inside Uganda," Culture and Information Minister Al-Tayeb Ibrahim Mohamed Khair was quoted in the government Al-Sudan al-Hadith newspaper as saying.
Khair, who is also the official spokesman, said the heavy weapons being massed at the border included tanks, long-range artillery and mortars.

"The expectations are that these forces are targeting the areas from Kapoeta in the east to Kaya in the west," he said, adding that the troops would also probably attack the key southern city of Juba.

Rebel leader John Garang said in remarks published in the Egyptian daily Al-Ahram on Sunday that his forces control 80 percent of southern Sudan and that "the government only has control over a few key towns such as Juba, Wau and Malakal."
The Sudanese government denies the rebel reports and there was no independent confirmation. The accuracy of reports issued by both sides in the conflict cannot be verified.

Sudan says that Ethiopian and Eritrean troops are fighting with rebels in the south and east, charges that both countries deny. The rebels say that they alone are behind the clashes that began early last month and that their aim is to put pressure on the government and spark a popular uprising.
Sudanese President Omar Hassan al-Bashir has said that he expects a third front to open on the Uganda border but that Sudan would not attack Uganda unless it was attacked first.
On Thursday, Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni told reporters that both states were "on the brink of war" and charged Sudan with supporting rebels fighting in the north.

Both countries have in the past readied themselves for an attack over heated charges that they support opposition groups. They signed a peace deal last year after Iranian mediation but relations have remained tense.
"With the Sudanese, we have run out of solutions...so I think now they will get a solution on the battlefield. That's what they've been waiting for," he told a news conference.
But a senior Uganda source said later: "We have no intention of invading Sudan. But if they choose to invade us we will be able to show them it was not the best option."

Khair said that Sudan was respecting the peace deal but that its army was ready to repulse and aggression. He also cautioned that Cairo was probably hatching a plot against Sudan after a senior opposition leader visited the disputed border area of Halaib with Egyptian officials.
Egypt and Sudan in the past have almost come to blows over the supposedly mineral-rich area of Halaib.

"At the end of last week, Mohammed Osman al-Mirghani paid a visit to Halaib area in the company of a senior Egyptian officer. This has probably a connection with the plots being implemented against Sudan," Khair said.

Mirghani is the head of the opposition Democratic Unionist Party, which is part of the umbrella National Democratic Alliance. Both Egyptian and party officials were not immediately available for comment.
Egypt's relations with Sudan have been strained over allegations that Khartoum trains the Moslem miliants who want to topple the Cairo government.
Ties worsened after three gunmen tried to kill Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak in Ethiopia in 1995. Egypt says the gunmen are hiding in Sudan while Khartoum denies the charges.
